newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Golf-Parsons and O'Malley grab Masters spotlight.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Parsons and O'Malley grab Masters spotlight.

text.p: Lucas Parsons and Peter O'Malley threatened to turn the Australian Masters golf tournament into a private duel by moving four shots clear after the second round on Friday.
The Australian pair were locked together on 15 under par for an aggregate score of 131 at the par-73 Huntingdale layout.
American Tiger Woods proved a surprising exception on a day of low scoring when he added a lacklustre 70 to his first round 68 to fall seven shots behind the leaders.
Parsons, who equalled the course record with 64 on Thursday, fired five successive birdies at the start of the back nine on his way to a second round 67.
O'Malley, a frequent competitor on the European PGA Tour, added a 66 to his first round 65 in a performance he later described as the best of his career over the first 36 holes.
Canadian Rick Gibson and Australian Shane Tait share third place on the leaderboard on 11 under par.

Woods, 21, who won the Bangkok Classic in Thailand on Sunday, his fourth tournament victory since turning professional last August, described the Huntingdale layout as "very difficult" despite the abundance of low scores.

"The greens are very hard to read and you must drive the ball in the fairway -- it is an absolute must," said Woods, who marred his round with successive bogeys on the last two holes for a share of ninth place.
"I am not happy with that finish but at the half-way point you want to be in the hunt and I'm right there."
Parsons said the conditions were perfect for scoring.
"The greens are bouncy by if you hit a crisp shot, the ball will stop. That is the reason for the scores," he said.
